---
description: "Use when adding or changing user-visible app copy, translation catalogs, copy references, or localization tooling."
applyTo: "src/**/*.ts,src/**/*.tsx,src/**/*.module.css,src/i18n/locales/**/*.json"
---
# App copy and localization

- Treat `docs/i18n.md` as the repository contract for app copy.
- Put every new static user-visible string in the modular English catalogs
  under `src/i18n/locales/`. Do not introduce a new raw JSX, config, label,
  description, state, error, placeholder, accessibility, modal, or navigation
  literal.
- Use the project facade from `src/i18n/`:
  - `useCopy(namespace)` in React components and hooks;
  - `copy(namespace, key, values)` in non-React code;
  - `copyRef(namespace, key, values)` for declarative configuration resolved
    at render time.
- Do not import `i18next` or `react-i18next` directly outside `src/i18n/`, and
  do not delegate app copy to HAKit or Home Assistant `localize()`.
- Reuse an existing semantic key when the meaning is identical. Otherwise add
  a lower-camel semantic key to the narrowest shared, page, feature, shell,
  core, or modal namespace.
- Preserve named `{{placeholders}}` exactly and use i18next plural families
  such as `_one` and `_other`. Never construct translated sentences by
  concatenating fragments.
- Keep live Home Assistant friendly names, task text, recipe content, provider
  data, and other user/backend values outside catalogs; interpolate them into
  static catalog copy.
- Keep Home Assistant notification delivery and notification source wording
  HA-owned. React catalogs may describe notification-linked UI, but must not
  become a notification producer.
- Keep wording tests independent: assert rendered English instead of importing
  the same catalog value into both production code and the assertion.
- Do not put user-visible text in CSS `content`; render catalog-backed copy in
  the component instead.
- After catalog or source migrations, run `npm run i18n:sync`,
  `npm run i18n:check`, and `npm run test:i18n`.
- Never use `--refresh-baseline` to approve new raw copy. It is reserved for an
  intentional scanner-rule change followed by review of the complete
  regenerated inventory.
